free_tier.stated: A 30 GB, 7-day try-out: 'The try out plan gives you: 500 mbit speed, 4084 days retention, 30 gigabytes free, No auto billing, Absolutely free'. The vendor's payment FAQ repeats it: 'Can I try your service before I pay? Hell yes! You can always try the first 7 days for free.'

per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: 4085 days retention on the home page, 4084 days on the try-out page

egress.terms: Unlimited speed on Senior; 40 Mbit on Junior and 80 Mbit on Medior

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563; no HTTP or object API exists for the download path, so a user drives it through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: A 30 GB Abavia allowance tests whether an Abavia spool completes a user's content before any money is spent; after that the Junior tier keeps it for EUR 2.46/mo.

limits.value: 25 connections on Junior and Medior, 50 on Senior
40 Mbit Junior, 80 Mbit Medior, unlimited Senior
30 GB on the free try-out, then unlimited on paid plans

limits_note: Junior EUR 2.46/mo (40 Mbit, 25 connections), Medior EUR 3.69/mo (80 Mbit, 25 connections), Senior EUR 5.75/mo (unlimited speed, 50 connections). No automatic renewal: 'Your subscription expires when your subscription days have passed.'
binding_note: The free path is a 30 GB one-off, so at 1 TiB/month the allowance is what fails, and it fails after 30 GB. On Senior the vendor publishes no volume ceiling.

identity_cost.detail: An email address, and the trial has three explicit gates: 'You can't register with a disposable e-mail address', 'You can't use a VPN or proxy server to register' and 'You can't have multiple accounts'. The VPN ban means the signup must come from a user's real residential address.

reliability_note: The try-out page also carries the line 'Payment will show up on your statement as NectoFarm B.V.', which is odd for a product listed at 'Total cost: FREE' and suggests a payment method may still be captured. That was not tested at checkout, so it is flagged rather than resolved. Abavia reseller operated by NectoFarm BV. The 30 GB try-out is the largest card-free allowance found on any provider, and the VPN ban is the price of it.
confidence_note: The trial terms, the three registration rules, the prices and the retention figure are all from vendor pages read. Whether a card is captured at checkout is the one gap, because the signup form itself was not opened.

evidence.proved: '30 gigabytes free', 'No auto billing', 'Absolutely free'; 7 days; 500 mbit; 4084 days; 'You can't use a VPN or proxy server to register'; 'Total cost: FREE'
Junior EUR 2.46/mo 40 Mbit 25 connections; Medior EUR 3.69/mo 80 Mbit 25 connections; Senior EUR 5.75/mo unlimited 50 connections; 4085 days
'Can I try your service before I pay? Hell yes!'; 'It is possible to set an automatic payment? We choose not to.'

notes: The caveat is the identity gate rather than the product: no disposable email, no VPN or proxy at signup, one account. A client behind a VPN cannot claim this trial at all.
